text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- National Assembly votes first part of bill creating pension funds for salaried workers. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- Former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing says the franc is overvalued against the dollar because of its parity with the mark, calls for a competitive depreciation, wins approval of Parliament speaker Philippe Seguin. German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Prime Minister Alain Juppe reaffirm their committment to a single european currency, while bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet issues warning against an unjustified devaluation. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation)
-- Truck drivers and employers negotiate for improved working conditions.
-- Credit Agricole to rely on its 51 percent owned unit Banque Indosuez to tackle large firms and international clients.
-- Groupe Rivaud starts to simplify its structure, its Compagnie du Cambodge launches buyout offer on two other subsidiaries, Mines de Kali and Caoutchoucs de Padang.
-- Senate majority calls for a lighter tax on wealthy taxpayers.
-- Lagardere Groupe to start legal action retaliating against a minority shareholder who criticises the terms of a 1990 Matra-Hachette merger.
-- Water suppliers Lyonnaise des Eaux and Generale des Eaux tackle Asia's water supply market.
-- Monday's fire in Eurotunnel channel tunnel triggers losses.
-- Trucks drivers carry on with demonstrations and road blocking.
-- Devaluation call from former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing causes franc to weaken.
